body_ar: بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم الحمد لله رب العالمين وأصلي وأسلم على من بعث رحمة للعالمين وعلى آله وأصحابه ومن اهتدى بهديه واستن بسنته إلى يوم الدين، السلام عليكم ورحمة الله وبركاته، أما بعد فإن الله تعالى أنزل القرآن على محمد (ص) بلسان عربي مبين، وقد جاء به جبريل عليه السلام إلى رسول الله (ص) منجما في ثلاث وعشرين سنة، ينزل بحسب الوقائع وبحسب ما يسأل عنه أهل الأرض وكان ذلك اتصالا بين أهل السماء وأهل الأرض، وارتباطا بين الخلق والخالق، جل وعلا ببيان ما يريده منهم وتشريع ما يرتضيه لهم، وقد ختم الله الرسائل إلى أهل الأرض برسالة محمد (ص)، وختم الكتب المنزلة إلى أهل الأرض بالقرآن، وجعله مصدقا لما بين يديه من الحق ومهيمنا على كل الكتب وناسخا لها، فلا يقبل الله من أحد بعد نزول القرآن دينا إلا هذا الإسلام الذي تضمنه هذا القرآن، وقد أنزل على هيآت متنوعة، فمنها أن يأتي الملك على هيئة رجل فيكلم رسول الله (ص) فيعي عنه ما يقول،
body_en:
In the name of God, the Most Merciful, the Compassionate. Praise be to God, Lord of the worlds. I invoke blessings and peace upon him who was sent as a mercy to the worlds, and upon his family and his Companions and whoever has taken his guidance for guidance and his sunnah for a way, until the Day of Judgement. Peace be upon you, and the mercy of God and His blessings.

To proceed: God, be He exalted, sent the Qur'an down upon Muhammad (peace and blessings be upon him) in a clear Arabic tongue. Gabriel (peace be upon him) brought it to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) in instalments over twenty-three years, coming down according to events and according to what the people of the earth asked about. That was a channel of contact between the people of heaven and the people of the earth, and a bond between the creation and the Creator — mighty and exalted is He — by the setting out of what He wants from them and the legislating of what He is content with for them. God sealed the messages to the people of the earth with the message of Muhammad (peace and blessings be upon him), and sealed the books sent down to the people of the earth with the Qur'an; and He made it confirming the truth that was before it, a guardian over all the books, and abrogating them. So God accepts from no one, after the descent of the Qur'an, any religion but this Islam which this Qur'an contains. It was sent down in a variety of modes: among them, that the angel would come in the form of a man and speak to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him), and he would retain from him what he said,

The published page carries only the opening excerpt of this tape; the Arabic breaks off and the full text is offered on the site as a downloadable Word document. The English ends exactly where the Arabic ends. Nothing has been supplied to complete it.

The Arabic breaks off mid-enumeration: the Sheikh announces that the Qur'an came down 'in a variety of modes' and the excerpt gives only the first before stopping. Nothing has been supplied for the remainder, and the English must not be read as a complete account of the modes of revelation.

al-Jazariyyah is the versified primer on Qur'anic recitation by Ibn al-Jazari, and 'the author' throughout this series is Ibn al-Jazari. The series title is left transliterated and untranslated. Articles 436-446 are tapes of this one series; their tape numbering in the titles does not run in the same order as the article IDs.
The source writes the honorific after the Prophet's name as the abbreviation (ص); it is rendered in full in the English as 'peace and blessings be upon him'.
